settled_2026_08_05.node_vs_leaf: TWO LAYERS, and every prior artifact in this ticket collapsed them into one. NODE = the thing being remembered: content, provenance, standing. It has an IDENTITY, it lives in the one node list per database, and it NEVER belongs to a tree. LEAF = the thing indexing it: it lives in a tree's own table at ADDRESS `database.tree.leaf`, points at a node, and carries weights and edges to other leaves. The address is a LOCATOR and changes when the tree reorganizes; the node's identity does not. One node can be indexed by many leaves in many trees — which is what makes 'two tree sets indexing one node set' a mechanism rather than a slogan. MEASURED AGAINST THE RUNNING STORE 2026-08-05: cairn/devices/librarian/trees.py is ONE table (node_id, tree, content, vector, provenance, standing, created) with no link columns of any kind. That row is a node and a leaf collapsed together, which is why its identity function `node_id = sha256(tree + content)` binds the remembered thing to a tree. That is not a hash bug to patch — it is the collapsed row showing through, and it contradicts 'one node list per database' directly. The leaf layer is a PREREQUISITE for calving, not a consequence of it: there is currently nothing to renumber and nowhere for an edge to live.
settled_2026_08_05.the_shear__answers_open_question_2: AKIEN, same turn: 'a leaf points to a node, and has edges that point to other leaves, WHO ALSO POINT BACK.' Edges are TWO-WAY, and that is what makes the shear tractable: a moved leaf's IN-LINK LIST IS the exact set of holders of stale pointers, so the affected set is ADDRESSABLE, not merely small. One-way, that set exists but has no address and you find it by reading every leaf's out-links in the database — which is the searching the whole addressing design exists to eliminate, reappearing in the reverse direction. CC's arithmetic, UNMEASURED: bound B, corpus N, so ~N/B calves over the corpus's life. One-way = an O(N) scan per calve = O(N^2 g / B) total. Two-way = O(B g) per calve = O(N g) total. At B=5,000 and N=2.5M that is ~500 calves: order 10^9 row-touches against order 10^6 edge-entry rewrites. Quadratic versus linear — and the quadratic version gets expensive exactly as the corpus grows large enough to need calving. SECOND PROPERTY, and the one that matters for Law 7: calving is a PURE LEAF OPERATION. Nodes are not read and not written. Index maintenance can never damage a record of truth, because it never touches one. Reorganize the trees as often as you like; provenance cannot drift, because it is not in the layer that moves.
settled_2026_08_05.edges__answers_open_question_3: SETTLED BY THE SHEAR, not by preference. Both kinds exist and the shear is the boundary: an edge that must survive a renumbering is an edge you are STORING; an edge you regenerate is one you are not. ARTICULATED edges — leaf to leaf, directed, stored, two-way — are what a shear fixes. SIMILARITY edges are derived from leaf vectors at walk time, never materialized, so a shear does not touch them and the next walk recomputes them against whatever the tree now holds. That gives the clean rule: EDGES ARE A PROPERTY OF THE INDEX, NEVER OF THE REMEMBERED THING. Nodes have no edges at all. Cost check on why the split is forced: a 5,000-leaf tree calving in half moves 2,500 leaves; at articulated degree ~4 that is ~10,000 entry rewrites, against 2,500 x 5,000 = 12.5M if similarity edges were materialized at full density.
settled_2026_08_05.the_vector_is_the_path: AKIEN, 2026-08-05: 'the vector becomes the path walked.' Precisely: the path is neither stored nor looked up — the query vector RUN AGAINST THE ATTRACTORS generates the route, and the sequence of choices IS the path. Two decisions: which tree (compare against each tree's dominant attractor), then which leaves within it. CC's arithmetic at d=768 float32, N=2.5M leaves, B=5,000 so ~500 trees: flat over all leaves touches 2.5M x 768 x 4 = 7.7 GB per query; two-level touches 500 x 768 x 4 = 1.5 MB of attractors plus 5,000 x 768 x 4 = 15 MB of one tree = ~16.5 MB. The ratio (~470x) is not the point — the point is that 7.7 GB per query fits nowhere and 16.5 MB sits in cache and stays hot. CONSEQUENCE, and it reframes calving: calving along dominant attractors is THE OPERATION THAT CREATES THE PATH. Before the first calve a tree is flat and there is no route to walk, only a scan. Each calve mints an attractor, and the attractor is what a query steers by. The walk-cost bound is a side effect of building structure, not the reason for it. A tree therefore needs a dominant-attractor vector of its own — a tree-level structure trees.py has no place for today. Flat-over-trees stays fine for a long time: 500 attractors is 1.5 MB, and a tree OF trees is not wanted until ~100K trees (~500M leaves).
settled_2026_08_05.the_measured_history_that_motivates_all_: AKIEN, 2026-08-05 — the number this ticket was missing. The conventional build (SQLite, conventional tables, a stored edge table) reached 70,000 words and 2.5M BIGRAM EDGES, and EVERY SINGLE EDGE UPDATE TOOK OVER 30 SECONDS. So the 2.5M in the falsifier below is not a projection: it is the corpus size at which the previous build died. The mechanism: ingesting one memory means many UPDATEs against a 2.5M-row edge table, each an index seek or a scan, each taking a write lock, each syncing — and THE COST GROWS WITH THE CORPUS. The system got slower exactly as it learned more. Postgres buys perhaps an order of magnitude and then meets the same wall, because the wall is storing edges at all. THE TRADE THE DESIGN MAKES: stored edges pay at WRITE time and the price grows with the corpus; derived edges plus bounded trees pay at READ time and the price is capped by the bound rather than by how much has been learned. Adding a memory writes one node row and one leaf row; no similarity edge is updated, because none exists to update.
settled_2026_08_05.build_order_for_the_embeddings_generator: AKIEN'S FRAMING, 2026-08-05: 'we HAD (UU) an embeddings generator that would take the text of a memory into the device, and out would pop embeddings by following the graph trees. So the question becomes: what do we need to make that work?' CC's answer, in build order, each step usable before the next exists: (1) THE LEAF LAYER — `nodes` (one list per database, content-addressed, tree-free) split from `leaf_<tree>` (address, node pointer, vector, weights, edges). Everything below needs it first. (2) TREE ATTRACTORS — each tree carries the centroid of its leaves so a query can pick a tree before touching leaves; without it every walk compares against every leaf in every tree, which is the 2.5M problem in a new hat. (3) A SEED EMBEDDER — text must become some vector to enter the walk; this is the only place a model is required and its job is only to land in roughly the right tree, so it can be small, local, and reached through inference_domain. (4) THE WALK — seed vector to nearest tree attractors (probe the top few, not the top one), then leaves within, ranked. Its output is the path. (5) THE COMPOSER — turn the walked path into the output embedding; simplest version that works is a similarity-weighted mean of the walked leaves' vectors. This is the step that makes it 'embeddings by following the graph trees' rather than embeddings from a model, and it is where the bootstrap resolves: the seed gets you in the door, the composition is the real representation, and the composed vector is what gets stored. (6) THE WRITE PATH — deposit the node (dedupe on content, globally), mint a leaf in the tree the walk landed in carrying the composed vector. (7) CALVING AND THE SHEAR — only needed once a tree exceeds the bound, so it can wait until data demands it, by which time the walk will have shown where the real attractors are instead of us guessing. DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS LIST, both reversible: articulated edges and leaf weights. A walk composes from geometry alone; edge weights (paths that resolve get stronger) are a real mechanism and the natural correction for a bad router, but they are the second build.

[CORPUS] NODE -> LEAF BACK-REFERENCE. Akien's two-way principle bites one layer up too: 'where is this node indexed?' — needed for invalidation when standing changes — is otherwise a lookup against every tree table (~500 of them at 2.5M leaves). Storing the leaf list on the node makes it one read, but then a shear DOES touch nodes, one entry per moved leaf, and the 'calving never writes a node' property above holds only if this back-reference does not exist. Two real options, both cheap, and the choice is the corpus's: stored back-reference, or a per-tree index on leaf.node_id queried across trees.

[CORPUS] CROSS-TREE IN-LINKS ARE CROSS-OWNER WRITES — what remains of the original shear question. If a leaf in tree B points at a leaf in tree T, T's calve must rewrite a row B's owner gates, and under Law 6 the shear cannot reach in. Two-way makes this TRACTABLE (T knows exactly who to notify) but not free: the fixup has to travel through B's gate. Narrowed from 'how do we find them' to 'how is the notification gated'.

[CORPUS] THE MUTUAL INVARIANT NEEDS ONE DOOR. If a link's out-half and in-half can be written separately they can drift, and a drifted back-reference means the shear misses a leaf — whose stale pointer then does not dangle but SILENTLY RETARGETS to whatever now occupies that address. That is a record of truth quietly saying something false (Law 7). So one operation writes both halves or the link does not exist (Law 4 shape), and the falsifier is 'an out-link with no mirror in-link exists'. Cheap belt-and-braces regardless: never reuse leaf numbers after a shear, so a missed pointer dangles loudly instead of retargeting silently.

[MEASUREMENT] MANUFACTURED NOVELTY — a NEW failure mode that falls out of the two-level walk, and the exact twin of the home-field finding. If the router picks the wrong tree the walk misses, and a miss fires the backfill — so A ROUTING ERROR IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM GENUINE NOVELTY. The system mints nodes for something it already knows, filed in the wrong neighbourhood, and the mint then wins the similarity race for its own question. Manufactured RESOLUTION is a high score that is not evidence; manufactured NOVELTY is a miss that is not absence, and it is worse because it is self-reinforcing: each routing miss deposits more nodes that make the wrong tree slightly more attractive. Softener: probe the top-k trees rather than the top one (k=5 costs 75 MB instead of 15 MB — nothing). Measurement: router recall@k, by taking queries whose correct leaf is known and checking whether the router lands on its tree.

[MEASUREMENT] DOES THE COMPOSER EARN THE WALK? Steps 3-5 of the build order make a testable claim: THE COMPOSED EMBEDDING IS BETTER THAN THE SEED EMBEDDING. If walking the trees does not produce a better representation than the cheap model you entered with, then for THIS purpose the trees are decoration — they would still earn their keep as a cache, but 'embeddings by following the graph trees' would be false. Check it BEFORE step 6, not after: take text whose correct node is known, compute both vectors, see which retrieves it. Costs one afternoon; if composed wins, it is the strongest measured thing the design has.

[AKIEN+RESEARCH] HOW DOES A WEIGHT CHANGE? REFRAMED 2026-08-21 by Akien: 'maybe it's not how fast, it's proven and disproven? and in fact, maybe the right answer to how fast is: how does the biology do it? let's examine that.' BIOLOGY RESEARCH 2026-08-21 — the biology DOES support the reframe, and reveals THREE states not two: (1) PROVEN (consolidated via synaptic tagging + protein capture + replay — a structural change that persists until actively contradicted), (2) DISPROVEN (active LTD — counter-evidence arrived, the path is actively weakened, FAST), (3) UNPROVEN (tagged but never confirmed — decays passively, no counter-evidence needed, absence of confirmation is sufficient). The key asymmetry: STRENGTHENING REQUIRES ACTIVE CONFIRMATION, WEAKENING IS THE DEFAULT. For the home-field problem the biology has three overlapping defenses: homeostatic scaling (total weight per leaf is bounded — maps to a normalization constraint), metaplasticity/BCM rule (strengthening gets harder as weight grows — diminishing returns), and mismatch detection (wrong content on a route actively depresses that route — maps to the sieve's own feedback). The biological mechanism (STDP) directly converts traversal frequency into stored weight, validating Akien's stored-weights position. Full research at scratchpad/biology-weight-decay.md. AKIEN'S DECISION is still open: which of these three mechanisms (or what combination) to adopt for the graph trees.
